Frequently asked questions

Emergency help

How quickly can you get to me?

Because we’re based right here locally, we can usually be at your front door within 30 to 45 minutes for emergencies. When you call, you’ll speak directly to me, not a distant call centre, so I can give you an accurate arrival time based on where my team or I are at that moment.

Will you damage my door or frame to get me back in?

In the vast majority of cases, no. We always use non-destructive entry techniques first. Our goal is always to get you back inside safely without damaging your door or fitting a new lock unless it’s strictly necessary or already broken.

It’s midnight or a bank holiday—do you actually answer?

Yes! Emergencies don’t stick to 9-to-5 hours, so neither do we. Whether it’s 2 AM on a rainy Sunday or a bank holiday afternoon, if you’re locked out, just give us a call.

Pricing & payment

How much is this going to cost? Are there hidden call-out fees?

We don’t believe in surprise bills. We never charge a call-out fee. Guide prices are available upfront, and we will always give you the exact fee before starting any work so you know where you stand.

What payment methods do you accept?

Whatever is easiest for you on the doorstep! We accept debit and credit cards, contactless, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and cash. (Bitcoin payment coming soon! 😉)

Moving home & door repairs

We just moved into a new house. Should we change the locks?

Congratulations on the new home! Yes, it’s always recommended. You never know how many spare keys were handed out to estate agents, previous tradespeople, or past neighbours over the years. We can pop by, assess your current locks, and upgrade them to British Standard locks in a single visit.

My uPVC door handle is stiff or stuck. Do I need a whole new door?

Almost never! A stiff or sticking handle usually means the internal multipoint gearbox mechanism needs adjusting or replacing. Replacing or servicing the internal mechanism is far cheaper and quicker than buying a whole new door.
